codeQuality.summary: This payment processing module has critical PCI-DSS compliance violations including handling raw credit card data, CVV storage potential, and insufficient audit logging. The lack of transaction atomicity means users could be charged without receiving their subscription. This code should NOT be deployed to production without significant security remediation.

testCoverage.summary: This payment processing module has ZERO test coverage. All 6 functions handling payment validation, card charging, pricing calculations, and subscription management are completely untested. This is unacceptable for financial transaction code.

refactorings.summary: Major architectural issues stemming from tight coupling between business logic and data access. Highest-impact refactorings: (1) Repository Pattern for testability, (2) PaymentValidator class extraction, (3) Configuration externalization.

recommendations.description: This PR introduces payment processing that violates PCI-DSS requirements by handling raw credit card data. CANNOT be deployed to production in current form.
No transaction wrapping. If subscription update fails after charge succeeds, customer is charged but receives no service, creating chargebacks.
No rate limiting enables card testing attacks. No idempotency enables duplicate charges on retries.
Zero test coverage on critical payment processing. Unacceptable for production code handling financial transactions.
Insufficient input validation and unsafe JSON parsing without try-catch.
SELECT * violates least privilege. Could leak future sensitive data.
Business logic tightly coupled with data access prevents testing without real database.
Pricing tiers and features hardcoded. Changes require redeployment.
